summary: IPSec VPN path strips TCP options (timestamps/ECN) causing TLS session-resume fallback and intermittent gRPC streaming pauses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinSight runs Redwood Private in their on-prem environment peered to our control plane via an IPSec tunnel over a Transit Gateway. They report intermittent gRPC streaming pauses and elevated tail latency on chat streams.

Impact:
- Intermittent stalls in streaming responses for user-facing chat: approx 3-7% of requests in the last 24h experienced a streaming pause (~5-20s) followed by resume or full reconnect.
- Increased token cost due to repeated model pulls in a few cases where stream reconnect triggered a model cold-start.
- Visible in customer metrics and SRE dashboards as higher 99th pct latency and small spike in TLS full-handshake rate.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed) peered via IPSec site-to-site tunnel to our us-east-1 control plane peering.
- Customer NGFW: Palo Alto PA-5220 (managed by customer security team).
- Transit Gateway in customer account doing route propagation.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Run a sustained streaming chat workload to the customer's private endpoint (~100 concurrent streams).
2) After ~3-6 minutes, a subset of streams pause mid-response for several seconds then either resume or reconnect.
3) Examine flow logs and capture tcpdumps on customer-side gateway and on the Private deployment host.

Logs / Evidence:
- tcpdump (customer side) shows SYN/SYN-ACK and then data flows where TCP Timestamp and ECE/CWR option bytes are missing for affected flows.
- Packet captures from private host show TLS session ticket issued by control plane but client attempts session-resume are rejected by control plane with 'unsupported_session' in TLS-level logs.
- SRE dashboard (tracing) shows increase in TLS full handshakes concurrent with streaming pauses.
- VPC flow logs show no route flips; no MTU icmp-unreach seen.
- Customer firewall logs indicate IPSec reassembly performed and 'normalize-tcp-options' policy applied.

Immediate customer impact: degraded real-time UX for end-users; customer flagged as high priority due to production traffic and enterprise SLAs.
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Customer NGFW normalization policy strips TCP options (timestamps/ECN) which alters endpoint TCP behavior and triggers control plane TLS session-resume validation failure on our side (we check session tickets + connection metadata).
- Hypothesis 2: Option stripping leads to subtle differences in TCP segmentation/timestamp behavior that cause reordering and trigger server-side TLS stack to invalidate resumptions for security/performance reasons.
- Collected pcap pair: customer-gw-2026-03-11.pcap, private-host-2026-03-11.pcap (links shared in Slack #support-private).
- Correlated times with control-plane logs: control-plane shows ‘tls: resume fail: ticket-mismatch’ for the affected flows.
- Reproduced in staging by enabling a Palo Alto normalization policy that strips TCP timestamps; observed similar resume failure pattern.
- Engineering note: TLS session resumption in our stack records some connection-level metadata (ALPN, SNI, cipher) and also logs of 'observed tcp options' were added to help debug; mismatch currently causes us to fall back to full handshake but shouldn't pause gRPC streaming — pause appears related to keepalive handling during fallback.
- Customer disabled 'normalize-tcp-options' on a test tunnel and saw immediate reduction in streaming pauses during a 1h soak (failure rate dropped from ~4% to ~0.4%).

Cross-references:
- Slack: #support-private thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C03ABC123/p1678536000000
- PR adding tcp option logging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2148
- Runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/39823/Private+Deploy+VPN+Troubleshooting
resolution:
Workaround implemented: customer disabled 'TCP option normalization' policy on the IPSec path to our control plane; immediate improvement observed.

Permanent remediation options (next steps agreed with customer):
1) Customer: whitelist traffic to control plane and disable TCP option normalization for Redwood peer subnets (recommended).
2) Engineering: add more tolerant session-resume checks that do not require exact TCP option set parity and harden keepalive behavior so gRPC streams do not pause during fallback. PR #2148 adds tcp-option logs and a short-term heuristic to avoid pausing; follow-up PR will implement a safer resume-relax path.
3) Document: add a KB article for private customers describing NGFW rules that commonly cause streaming regressions (include Palo Alto example and recommended exclusions).

Status: Workaround accepted by customer; Engineering working on code changes (targeting canary next week). Postmortem and KB entry scheduled after code and doc rollout.
